suggested_services_note: Each row is one way this kind of work takes money (one of the master's 28 paths per flow). The owner keeps the services that fit and picks ONE path per service and place. Names and amounts are examples from the profession file, not prices.

suggested_services.name: Overnight Week 2
suggested_services.example: The main story: Ava's Overnight Week 2, Sat Oct 24 to Fri Oct 30 (fall break), $1,150. A $250 deposit is paid on the secure page when registering, and the $900 rest is charged to the saved card when the week is done (Rosie never charges the rest on a date by itself). Day camp weeks ($325, $75 deposit) and the two-week session ($2,150, $400 deposit) are paid this way too. The camp's dated refund schedule is its own signed terms, shown before paying.

before_times: each camper's age on the first day of the session, and the grade they finish in June (they set the session and the cabin group)
day camp or overnight, and which week
for an overnight week: girls' or boys' cabins
for a backyard camp: the home's town (the travel area; the street address goes on the secure page), and how many children and their ages
for a camp tour: who is coming, and the child's age
after_time: one cabin-mate request, kept where it fits
for day camp: who drops off and picks up most days
anything the counselors should know that isn't health, like a first time away from home
for a backyard camp: a shaded part of the yard, and a bathroom inside the children can use
secure_page_only: the parent or guardian's yes that they may register the child, and the camp's agreement and risk notice, signed for the child
the camper's full name and birth date, the home address and two emergency contacts
the health form, the shot record (or the papers the state's rules accept instead), and a medicine form for each medicine, signed where the camp asks
allergies, health needs and any custody order, for the camp nurse and the director only
the pick-up list: the adults who may take the child home, and anyone who may not, with a copy of any court order
a yes or no for photos of the child
the card for the deposit or the full price
intake_questions.who_may_book: a parent or legal guardian, 18 or older, registers a camper, signs and pays; a teen gets a link to send to a parent; for a backyard camp, the host parent books the week and each child's own parent fills that child's forms

stop.words: a child hurt, very sick or in danger right now; a child who is missing
a report of abuse or neglect at a camp
stop.say: If a child is in danger now, call 911. You can also call your state's child abuse hotline. A person on Rosie's team will follow up.
stop.booking: no booking in that chat; a person on Rosie's team follows up

go_on.words: an allergy, asthma, a medicine or a health need
go_on.what: the booking goes on; the details go on the secure page for the camp nurse; Rosie gives no health advice

go_on.words: a food allergy that needs an epinephrine pen
go_on.what: the booking goes on; the nurse reads the form before camp, and the pen comes to check-in in its labeled box

go_on.words: a custody order, or a person who may not pick up
go_on.what: the booking goes on; the order goes on the secure page for Sam and the check-in staff, never in a text

go_on.words: a first time away from home, or homesick worries
go_on.what: the booking goes on; the note goes to the head counselor on the secure page

safety_and_stop_words.always: the generic screen: danger to life, fire, gas, a medical emergency → call 911, and no booking

steps.name: The camp's agreement and risk notice
steps.when: signed on the secure page while registering
steps.who: a parent or guardian signs for the child
steps.result: signed: the booking goes on; not signed in 10 minutes: nothing is booked

steps.name: The pick-up list and the photo yes or no
steps.when: on the secure page while registering; the parent can change them until pick-up
steps.result: only adults on the list take the child home; no answer to photos counts as no

steps.name: Health form, shot record and medicine forms
steps.when: open when registering; due May 15 (the camp's setting; the state's rules can set more)
steps.who: the parent fills them; the camp nurse reads each one
steps.result: still missing: one reminder a week, then Sam calls; no camper checks in without them

steps.name: Backyard camp: each child's forms and the yard check
steps.when: each child's own parent fills that child's forms by 7 days before the first day; the host fills the yard check while booking
steps.result: the yard has a fence or a clear edge, shade, water and a bathroom inside; a pool is gated and locked; pets stay inside; a child with no forms doesn't join

first_steps_and_forms.prep: for the check-in note: the check-in window and the closing-day pick-up time; medicines in their original labeled boxes for the nurse; the camp's own packing list; photo ID for anyone picking up; for a backyard camp: the yard and the bathroom ready, pets inside, and each child's snack and water bottle

staff.skills: head counselor (a cabin group or a day camp group), counselor, camp nurse, waterfront staff, backyard camp counselor, party leader
staff.licenses_or_certificates: first aid and CPR for every counselor; a water safety certificate for anyone guarding the lake or pool; switches from the state's form, on by default
staff.supervision: two adults with any group of children; counselors under 18 never count toward the ratio
staff.who_oks: Sam OKs waitlist offers, moves after May 1, refunds and exceptions; Pat may OK waitlist offers and moves too, and Sam's answer wins; Hannah, the camp nurse, answers health questions
staff.ratio: 8 campers and 2 counselors a cabin; 10 campers and 2 counselors a day camp group; 6 children and 2 counselors at a backyard camp (the example camps' settings; a ratio from the state's form wins)

children_and_age.who_may_book: a parent or legal guardian, 18 or older, registers a camper, signs and pays; a teen gets a link to send to a parent; for a backyard camp, the host parent books the week and each child's own parent fills that child's forms
children_and_age.minors_texts: a teen gets a link to send to a parent; Rosie never texts a child

visit.check_in: overnight: on check-in day, the parent gives the camper's check-in code at the check-in table, the nurse takes any medicines and checks the forms, and the head counselor walks the camper to the cabin; day camp: each day the adult dropping off signs the camper in with the code, and signs out at pick-up; backyard camp: the code at the host's door on the first day, then each child signed in and out by their own adult each day; a camp tour: the code at the camp office
visit.done: the check-in code on the first day, the sign-out at closing-day pick-up, and the head counselor's DONE once every camper has gone home
visit.changes_at_visit: a cabin or counselor change inside the camp is the camp's own; a change of session or dates is texted to the parent with a yes first

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: from the state form: a youth camp license or permit for the camp's own grounds where the state's rules require one (a switch), renewed on the state's schedule; health inspections of the grounds, kitchen, water, cabins and swim area where the state's or county's rules require them (a switch); a backyard camp at a family's home may need none, or the host site's own OK (a switch)
license.who: the business, for the camp license, its inspections and its registration; the camp nurse, for a nursing license; each counselor, for first aid and CPR certificates; waterfront staff, for their own water safety certificates
license.ask: the camp license number and its end date where the state's form asks (shown in an obviously made-up example as EX-1042); the date of the last health inspection; the business registration; the camp nurse's license number; each person's first aid and CPR certificates; any accreditation the camp holds, only as the camp gives it
license.insurance: liability insurance where the state's form asks for it, or where a host site (a school, a park, a community center) asks for proof
license.background: a background check for every staff member and regular volunteer before they start, and again on the state's schedule, where the state's rules require it (a switch from the state's form, on by default for anyone who works with children): who ran it and when, kept on file, shown to families only as the camp's own dated statement

never_in_a_text: a child's last name, birth date, allergies, medicines, health needs, custody orders, the pick-up list (and who may not pick up) and photos never go in a text; texts to the parent may use the child's first name; texts to Sam or the staff carry none of it: they name the parent and the session, and link to the secure page
